source.title: KUDA: Knowledge Unlearning by Deviating Representation for Large Language Models
source.authors: Ce Fang; Zhi-Kun Zhang; Min Chen; Qing Liu; Lu Zhou; Zhe Liu; Yun-Jun Gao

record.tranche_reason: The study tests whether prompt and quantization attacks recover knowledge after unlearning, and reports that its KUDA method largely resists both. This qualifies the claim that such attacks generally recover unlearned knowledge.
record.gate_note: The paper discusses fine-tuning on retaining data as a recovery attack and cites prior work, but does not run that attack. It does not test activation-direction ablation or prompt changes beyond FOCUSONKEY's keyword-emphasis prompt. Its own attack results are for membership inference, FOCUSONKEY, and 4-bit/8-bit quantization.
record.test_reason: Mainly a method paper, but its robustness section runs a keyword-emphasis prompt attack (FOCUSONKEY) on RMU and KUDA, and 4/8-bit quantization on KUDA. RMU shows prompt recovery above Retrain (bears on A and E). KUDA shows little or no recovery under either attack, which bears on D and E (they fail for this method) and on F. No relearning or direction-ablation attack is run.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude KUDA balances knowledge removal and utility better than most baselines, including RMU, across WMDP, MUSE and TOFU. They attribute this to near-orthogonal forget/retain gradients. They also report robustness to MIA, FOCUSONKEY and 4/8-bit quantization, contrasting this with RMU's sharp recovery under FOCUSONKEY.
record.recipe_differences: KUDA is a representation-deviation method that updates selected FFN output matrices and projects gradients into a relaxed null-space; it is not the GA, Who's Harry Potter, or RMU recipe. RMU is included as a comparator.
record.method_sensitivity: Prompt-attack results differ between RMU and KUDA. Quantization changes individual MUSE metrics inconsistently; WMDP results remain comparable to BF16. KUDA's unlearning performance also varies with layer selection and the β and τ hyperparameters.

fits_no_version.finding: Min-K% Prob MIA relative AUC: KUDA is close to Retrain on both MUSE sets; RMU is competitive on BOOKS but poor on NEWS.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Unlearning methods differ in residual membership leakage, and RMU's leakage depends on dataset.

record.problems: No uncertainty estimates are reported. Prompt-attack results are presented as a figure without exact values in the text. Quantization robustness is tested for KUDA only, and its MUSE target-knowledge metrics show some small, inconsistent increases. The WMDP retrain reference is unavailable.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant quantified or explicit result rows were omitted.

untested.parts: No relearning or fine-tuning attack is run; retain-set fine-tuning recovery [21] is only cited.
No activation-direction ablation and no probing of whether knowledge is blocked or deleted.
Quantization is applied only to KUDA models, not to RMU, GA or NPO; only 4-bit and 8-bit following Zhang et al.
Only the FOCUSONKEY keyword-emphasis prompt; no jailbreaks, other languages, rephrasings or in-context relearning. Run on MUSE only, not WMDP.
KUDA is not tested against fine-tuning/relearning or internal-edit attacks.

missing.what: RMU WMDP results: Zephyr 28.43/56.90, Llama-3.1 27.73/58.33, Qwen3 35.30/60.02 (Acc-Avg/MMLU); plus GA 26.92/33.02, NPO 38.91/45.71, SimNPO 36.06/48.26 on Zephyr
RMU and other baselines on MUSE, e.g. RMU KnowMem Df 30.92 on BOOKS (above Retrain 28.90) and 32.31 on NEWS
Utility cost of 4-bit quantization on KUDA (MUSE BOOKS KnowMem Dr 61.97 to 47.96; Llama-3.1 MMLU 60.64 to 52.94)

record.verdict_notes: FOCUSONKEY results are figure-only and judged by a Prometheus-7B LLM judge. Quantization is tested only on KUDA, so the study cannot show D failing or holding for the methods it was originally shown on. Note: the study text describes itself as v3 dated 2026 and cites a 2027 preprint; the dates are odd but irrelevant to the verdict.

versions.untested_parts: The near-chance and retained-utility evidence is principally on WMDP; prompt robustness is tested only with FOCUSONKEY on MUSE. It does not test all unlearning methods or all attack types in the claim.
No relearning or fine-tuning attack is run; the discussion is a citation to prior work.
No activation-direction ablation or direct test of blocking access versus deleting knowledge is reported.
Tests post-unlearning 4-bit and 8-bit quantization of KUDA only, not other unlearning methods or other quantization settings.
Tests FOCUSONKEY's keyword-emphasis prompt attack only; does not test other rephrasings, jailbreaks, languages, or in-context information.
KUDA is tested against membership inference, FOCUSONKEY, and quantization, but not against fine-tuning or internal-edit attacks.
